title: 1954 AHSME Problem 9
statement: A point \(P\) is outside a circle and is \(13\) inches from the center. A secant from \(P\) cuts the circle at \(Q\) and \(R\) so that the external segment of the secant \(\overline{PQ}\) is \(9\) inches and \(\overline{QR}\) is \(7\) inches. The radius of the circle is:

solutions.text:
The power of \(P\) is \[ PQ\cdot PR=9(16)=144. \] It is also \(13^2-r^2,\) so \(169-r^2=144.\) Hence \(r^2=25\) and \(r=5\) inches.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The secant power is the external length times the whole secant length
